name: School Inspection Checklist
description: A facility inspection checklist covering safety, maintenance, compliance and grounds.

items.text: Test fire alarms and smoke detectors.
Inspect extinguishers for charge, tags and access.
Check sprinkler and suppression systems.
Confirm emergency lighting and exit signs work.
Verify exits and fire doors open and latch.
items.note: Confirm no exits are blocked or chained.

items.text: Check first-aid kits and AED units are stocked.
Inspect the roof, gutters and ceilings for leaks.
Check HVAC operation and replace filters.
Test plumbing for leaks and water pressure.
Inspect electrical panels, outlets and wiring.
Check doors, windows and locks for function.
Examine floors, stairs and railings for damage.
Confirm permits and certificates are current.
Review inspection records and prior findings.
Check accessibility features meet requirements.
Verify safety data sheets are accessible.
Confirm occupancy limits and signage are posted.
Log all findings with date and assigned owner.
Inspect restrooms for cleanliness and supplies.
Check kitchen and cafeteria food-safety conditions.
Confirm trash and waste are managed properly.
Look for signs of pests or infestation.
Verify cleaning chemicals are stored safely.
Check ventilation and air quality in key areas.
Inspect playground equipment for damage and wear.
Check walkways and parking for trip hazards.
Confirm exterior lighting works after dark.
Examine fencing, gates and perimeter security.
Clear drainage and check for standing water.
Verify signage and markings are visible.

faq.q: How often should a school be inspected?
faq.a: Run routine internal inspections on a set schedule, often monthly for general walkthroughs and more frequently for safety systems. Formal compliance inspections follow local regulations. Regular self-checks help you pass official inspections and avoid surprise failures.

faq.q: What should a facility inspection cover?
faq.a: A thorough inspection covers safety systems like alarms and extinguishers, building maintenance such as roofs, plumbing and HVAC, regulatory compliance and permits, sanitation, and the outdoor grounds. Documenting each area creates a record for planning and accountability.

faq.q: Why is documentation important during inspections?
faq.a: Written records show conditions over time, prove due diligence, support budgeting for repairs, and are often required for compliance. Logging each finding with a date and owner ensures issues get assigned and resolved rather than forgotten after the walkthrough.

Internal inspections are usually led by facilities managers or a designated staff member, sometimes with a committee. Specialized systems, such as fire suppression, elevators, or boilers, require certified professionals on a regulated schedule.

faq.q: Is this school inspection checklist available as a printable PDF?
faq.a: Yes. You can print it or download it as a PDF for facilities staff to carry on walkthroughs, then tick off each item and record any repairs or compliance items that need follow-up.
